name: managed-remote-access-credential-taxonomy
description: Credential taxonomy for the managed remote-access lane (merge unit A, TASK-5771). Every credential class is specified by issuer, subject/audience, storage/custodian, lifetime, single-use/replay rules, rotation, revocation, and forbidden exposure. All example values are obvious non-secret placeholders of the form PLACEHOLDER_*; real credential material must never appear in fixtures, logs, errors, audit, or documentation. The local daemon bearer is a distinct class: it is generated and held on the home host, injected only by the connector on the final connector-to-127.0.0.1 hop, and must never appear in remote input, client, Services, Headscale, DERP, network, fixture secrets, logs, errors, or audit.

classes.name: Services account/session credential
classes.issuer: HappyRanch Services authentication (browser authorization code + PKCE; account design is separately founder-gated)
classes.subject_audience: the human user account; audience is HappyRanch Services APIs only
classes.storage_custodian: macOS Keychain on the signed client; never on a home host, never in the connector
classes.lifetime: minutes; refresh rotation with reuse detection
classes.replay_rules: refresh tokens are single-rotation and must be invalidated on reuse; access tokens are short-lived and never stored in logs
classes.rotation: refresh-before-expiry; rotated token families are invalidated on rotation detection
classes.revocation: Services session revocation denies new access immediately and invalidates refresh families

classes.name: One-use enrollment credential (Headscale pre-auth key)
classes.issuer: HappyRanch Services provisioning worker, one-operation cell-scoped capability
classes.subject_audience: one specific tenant cell enrollment endpoint; bound to tenant/home/device public identity
classes.storage_custodian: memory/transient response only; returned exactly once over authenticated TLS to the intended device
classes.lifetime: single use; expires in at most 10 minutes
classes.replay_rules: a redeemed, expired, or revoked credential must be rejected with the same category as an absent one (no existence oracle)
classes.rotation: every enrollment mints a fresh credential; never reused or reissued
classes.revocation: revoking an issued-but-unredeemed credential makes redemption fail closed

classes.name: Client node/device private key and identity
classes.issuer: client generates locally; public identity attested to Services
classes.subject_audience: the client installation (device_id); audience is the tenant cell control plane and the paired home
classes.storage_custodian: macOS Keychain / tsnet state with file protection on the signed client
classes.replay_rules: the private key never leaves the client; proofs derived from it carry nonce/timestamp windows and are single-use per challenge
classes.rotation: re-enroll with a fresh key pair; rotated keys must lose all previous authority
classes.revocation: device revocation expires the node, denies new sessions, and closes live sessions at every layer

classes.name: Connector device proof (home connector identity)
classes.issuer: connector generates locally at first install; proves home identity to Services through a short-lived home-enrollment ceremony
classes.subject_audience: the home connector installation (connector_id); audience is Services and the paired client
classes.storage_custodian: connector encrypted local store (OS credential storage where practical) with owner-only permissions
classes.lifetime: persistent; epoch/revision based, rotated by explicit re-enrollment
classes.replay_rules: proofs presented to the connector carry fresh nonce/timestamp windows; a captured proof without the private key is not replayable
classes.rotation: re-enrollment ceremony; old proof loses authority on rotation
classes.revocation: connector trust update with monotonic revocation epoch; connector denies and closes immediately on revocation

classes.name: Pairing authorization (client-to-home relationship)
classes.issuer: home owner explicit approval via Services; recorded as a signed trust update
classes.subject_audience: the specific (tenant, home, device) triple being paired; audience is the connector authorization verifier
classes.storage_custodian: connector encrypted local store (authorization epoch); Services registry desired state
classes.lifetime: until revoked or re-paired; carries authorization epoch and expiry
classes.replay_rules: pairing authorization is bound to device identity; a replayed old trust update with a lower epoch is rejected as rollback
classes.rotation: re-pairing ceremony replaces the authorization with a new epoch
classes.revocation: revoking pairing denies new requests and closes live streams before or atomically with network-node removal; never reports success early

classes.name: Policy/revocation material (trust updates and policy artifacts)
classes.issuer: HappyRanch Services policy compiler and revocation service; signed artifacts
classes.subject_audience: connector policy/revocation verifier; tenant cell policy compiler
classes.storage_custodian: connector encrypted local store for signed trust updates; cell-pinned policy artifact with signature/hash validation
classes.lifetime: epoch-based; current policy and revocation epoch must be present and current before any request is authorized
classes.replay_rules: stale, future, rollback, empty, or malformed policy is denied; the last valid non-expired policy is not a substitute for a missing current one beyond a separately approved bounded grace
classes.rotation: monotonic revocation_epoch; every policy artifact carries a revision and checksum
classes.revocation: revocation_epoch advance is the durable deny signal; connector denies/ closes before or atomically with node removal

classes.name: Local daemon bearer
classes.issuer: daemon runtime on the home host (existing token_file, 0600 perms; generated via secrets.token_urlsafe)
classes.subject_audience: local daemon HTTP routes on 127.0.0.1 only
classes.storage_custodian: existing home-only protected token file on the daemon host; read by the connector only for the final loopback hop
classes.lifetime: existing daemon token lifecycle; rotation remains a separate founder-gated decision
classes.replay_rules: the bearer is never transmitted by the connector over any network; remote requests never carry it
classes.rotation: rotate per existing daemon lifecycle; any change requires separate approval
classes.revocation: daemon-side token invalidation; connector fails closed when the bearer is unreadable or invalid
